chunks: From him, from Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Li'an with his wife. He said: 'The child is attached to its mother, and her maternal uncles inherit him, and he does not inherit them.' So I asked him about the man if he admits to having lied himself, he said: 'The child is attached to him.'

key_terms.إِنْ أَكْذَبَ نَفْسَهُ: if he admits to having lied
key_terms.يَلْحَقُ الْوَلَدُ: the child is attached (lineage is established)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance and lineage ruling for a child after Li'an if the husband admits he lied?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuances of Li'an, specifically addressing the reversal of lineage attribution when a husband retracts his false accusation. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the child's inheritance follows the established lineage, shifting from the maternal side to the paternal side upon the husband's admission of truth, thereby ensuring equitable distribution of inheritance rights.

en.hubeali: From him, from Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who cursed his wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The child would be attached to its mother, and his maternal uncles would inherit him, and he would not inherit them’. So I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man if he (admits) having lied himself, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The child is joined to him’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith and Wuhayb ibn Hafs from abu Basir who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who forms Mula ‘anah against his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘The child is joined with his mother and his maternal uncle inherits his legacy but he cannot inherit them. I then asked, ‘What happens if he calls himself a liar?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The child is joined with him.’”
